input.rationale: Section 1.4 is the only inbound grant to us (the other licence, at p0038, runs from us to HDI and is out of scope). The grant of "access to, and the right to use" HDI's hosting system and administration tools is limited to "the Company" alone: it names neither our affiliates nor contractors acting on our behalf, and gives no mechanism (e.g. written notice) to add them, so it fails even the fallback position. It is also silent on revocability, leaving HDI room to argue access may be withdrawn at will. Section 10.3 (Assignment) binds successors and assigns, so successor transfer is largely covered, but affiliate/contractor scope is not. We propose a short subsection extending the rights to affiliates and contractors, confirming they are not revocable at HDI's discretion (only for uncured material breach or on termination), and confirming successor transferability; affiliate coverage on prior written notice is offered as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Extend the Section 1.4 access/use rights to Company affiliates and contractors, make them non-revocable at will and transferable to a successor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the access and use rights in Section 1.4 to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, confirmed the rights are not revocable at HDI's discretion, and made them transferable to a successor to our business, consistent with our licence-scope position. If HDI prefers, we can accept affiliate coverage on prior written notice as a fallback.

ops.text: The rights of access and use granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 extend to the Company's affiliates (each entity controlling, controlled by, or under common control with the Company) and to contractors acting on the Company's behalf, and are transferable to any successor to all or substantially all of the Company's business or assets by merger, acquisition or sale. Such rights are not revocable at HDI's discretion and may be suspended or withdrawn only for a material breach by the Company that remains uncured thirty (30) days after written notice, or upon expiration or termination of this Agreement.
